summary.text: A root of a polynomial is an input value that makes its output equal 0, and it is also called a zero.
Solving an equation is the same as finding zeros: regroup every term on the left so it reads f(x) = 0, and the solutions are the zeros of f.
Counting complex roots with their multiplicities, a polynomial has as many roots as its degree.

facts.label: Graph meaning
facts.value: Real zeros are x-coordinates where the graph meets the x-axis

facts.label: Example roots
facts.value: f(x) = x² − 5 x + 6 has roots 2 and 3

facts.label: Root count
facts.value: At most the degree; equal when complex roots are counted

facts.label: Conjugate pairs
facts.value: Non-real roots of real-coefficient polynomials come in conjugate pairs

facts.label: Degree four or less
facts.value: All roots can be written algebraically in the coefficients

items.prompt: Why must a real polynomial of odd degree cross the x-axis at least once?

options.label: Its graph is continuous and changes sign, so it must pass through 0
Its graph always has a sharp corner at the axis
Odd numbers always have a value of 0 somewhere
Its coefficients must add up to zero

items.explain: Polynomials are continuous, so a graph changing from negative to positive, which always happens with odd degree, must cross zero.

items.prompt: A function’s graph meets the x-axis at x = 2 and at x = 5. What do those two x-values have in common?

options.label: The graph is at its highest there
The function’s output is 0 at each
They are the coefficients of the function
The function is not continuous there

items.explain: Where a real function’s graph meets the x-axis, the function attains the value 0.

items.prompt: You want to solve x² = 9 − 2x. How can you turn it into a root question?

options.label: Square both sides until x disappears
Replace x with 0 and compare the sides
Move every term to one side so it reads (something) = 0
Divide both sides by x and drop what is left

items.explain: Any equation can be rewritten as f(x) = 0 by regrouping all terms on the left, and its solutions are then the zeros of f.

items.prompt: A polynomial with real coefficients has a root that is not real. What must be true of its other roots?

options.label: Every other root is real
Its conjugate is also a root, since non-real roots pair up
The root must be repeated an even number of times
The polynomial has degree 1

items.explain: The non-real roots of polynomials with real coefficients come in conjugate pairs.

items.prompt: A polynomial of degree n shows fewer than n real roots on its graph. Where can the rest be?

options.label: They do not exist
They are hidden in the coefficients
Some may be non-real complex roots or repeated roots
The polynomial must have been written wrong

items.explain: A degree-n polynomial has n complex roots counted with multiplicities, so missing ones are complex or repeated.

items.prompt: A friend claims every real polynomial of even degree must cross the x-axis. Why is that wrong?

options.label: Even degree forces exactly two crossings
Even-degree graphs always sit above the axis
Only a degree of 1 can cross
Even-degree ones may have no real roots at all

items.explain: Real polynomials of odd degree must have a real root, whereas even ones may have none.
